Hi all. Still figuring out what to do with this subverse. I was surfing around looking for interesting public health content when I found this article about Tennessee's rising rates of Hepatitis C. That brought me to find this report which I believe the news article refers to. It is rather technical in nature, and difficult to read, but by having a forum to discuss, it would be interesting to engage with it.

This week's report (that link will be irrelevant next week, so here is a permalink PDF) includes a number of interesting topics:

  • Tomorrow is World Hepatitis C Day (link)
  • A nation-wide Hepatitis C Elimination Program is being launched (link)
  • Outbreak of Cryptosporidiosis Among Veterinary Medicine Students — Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, February 2015 (link)
  • A 19-year-old Colorado male committed suicide after ingesting a cannabis-infused edible (link)
  • An updated snapshot of age-adjusted cancer mortality rates in the United States (link)

In the future, I will try to figure out an easier way of formatting this information. I may have missed some of the articles from this week's report, because this is all manual so far. Thanks for reading, please comment below!

Microsoft Backtracks On Windows 10 Forced Updates
That's a relief. My low bandwidth cap basically meant no Windows 10 for me otherwise. I can't have software forcing itself down my connection.

I cannot imagine a company more out of touch with its userbase than Microsoft. They've done some sort of clueless cockup on almost every product release throughout their history. I just walked through an install of Windows 7 with a friend and suggested they kill the updates. Someone else said "No, no, you definitely want those.." and helpfully hit the "download later" button. A short time later, Windows decided to install some USB driver and then restart the computer, and a message "Updating! Do not touch your computer. Updated 1 of 143..." appeared, rendering the computer completely useless. At that point, the computer's owner realized how much he did not want the Mandatory Downtime feature. We powered the computer off, rebooted, and disabled the Windows Update service so that it wouldn't ever even check.

I read somewhere that Microsoft engineers are severely disconnected from the world due to their wealth/living spaces/job benefits. One telling clue is their update downloads and installation. You can see that their expectation is lightning fast download speeds and almost bleeding edge hardware.

What do you think software engineers should focus on? Do you think they should expect 128kbps connections? Should they expect users to investigate only the security patches that will effect them?

Automatic updates protect all of us as well as vaccines protect kids.

That statement has no meaning, basically GIGO... YES they should expect low speeds and Yes they should consider what patches are needed for certain machines/areas/etc. Software engineers need to be step out of the cocoon a bit because they are getting the above GIGO.

Disabling updates entirely is brain-dead. Set them to notify but not download\install. Choose a time when you're done on the computer and let it update then. Or you know, just be a member of a botnet in perpetuity.

The problem is that Microsoft's implementation of updates, even if you choose manual updates on notify is intolerably broken. The notification is monolithic, with no information about individual updates or what's being patched. The idea of a single group of "important" updates and you either download them all or not is an example of how Microsoft is out of touch not only with its userbase, but with basic OS usability design.

The only way that I can support people running Windows 7 or up is to shut it off. I put them behind NAT and install client side firewalls so keyloggers and botnets aren't an issue. It's been a piece of cake to convert people from Windows 8 to Ubuntu though. Anyone exposed to Windows 8 is soon begging for anything else, so I slap a copy of Ubuntu on their machine and all the support issues go away.

I feel like I must have missed something here. Is MS forcing you to take all or none of the "important" updates for win10? In win7 I go through the whole list of updates item by item, approving or disapproving as I go...

I don't know about Win10. I've never seen it and almost certainly never will. I know that I've never seen a list of individual updates and descriptions in Win7 though. What I've seen is either a "1 of X" display and the machine is then locked down and useless, requiring a hard power-off, or the user is sitting there late at night working, and suddenly from their perspective the machine hangs and they lose whatever they were working on.
